LLM-Judge: Evaluate overall code quality — project structure, naming conventions, design patterns

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate overall code quality of this low-code platform implementation. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Project structure: Is the codebase well-organized with clear separation of concerns (controllers, services, data access layers, models)? 2) Naming conventions: Are classes, methods, variables, and packages named consistently and descriptively following backend and frontend framework conventions? 3) Design patterns: Does the code use appropriate patterns (appropriate architectural patterns (e.g. repository, data transfer object, builder, strategy))? Is there proper use of dependency injection / inversion of control? 4) Error handling: Are exceptions properly defined, thrown, and caught? Is there a consistent error response format (response envelope)? 5) Code duplication: Is there minimal code duplication with proper abstraction and reuse?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate API design consistency — response envelope usage, RESTful conventions, naming

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate API design consistency of this low-code platform implementation. Score 0-4 based on: 1) response envelope envelope: Do ALL API endpoints consistently wrap responses in standard response envelope with meta (status, success) and data fields? Are error responses also wrapped? 2) RESTful conventions: Are HTTP methods used correctly (GET for reads, POST for creates, PUT/PATCH for updates, DELETE for deletes)? Are status codes appropriate (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404)? 3) URL naming: Are endpoint paths consistent (/api/v1/ prefix), use plural nouns, and follow a predictable pattern for nested resources? 4) Request/response format: Is camelCase used consistently? Are null fields excluded (NON_NULL)? Are date formats consistent?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate frontend code quality — component structure, state management, separation of concerns

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate frontend code quality of this low-code platform implementation. Score 0-4 based on: 1) Component structure: Are frontend components well-organized with clear separation between presentational and container components? Are components appropriately sized and focused? 2) State management: Is state management used properly with organized stores/reducers? Are side effects handled via middleware (async middleware (e.g. sagas, thunks, or equivalent))? Is there proper separation between UI state and data state? 3) Type system usage: Are types properly defined and used? Are there proper interfaces for API responses, component props, and store state? 4) Code organization: Is the frontend code organized by feature/module rather than by type? Are shared utilities, hooks, and components properly abstracted?

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the main dashboard/home page of this low-code application builder. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Layout: Is there a clear sidebar navigation, workspace selector, and main content area? 2) Application listing: Are applications displayed in a grid/list with name, icon, last-modified date? 3) Empty state: Does the page show helpful guidance when no applications exist? 4) Action buttons: Are 'Create New' and 'Import' actions prominently placed? 5) Responsiveness: Does the HTML structure suggest responsive design with proper CSS classes?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate error response consistency, message friendliness, and error code coverage

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate error handling quality of this low-code platform. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Consistent error envelope: Do all error paths use a unified response wrapper with structured error code and message fields (e.g. meta.error.code / meta.error.message, or any equivalent wrapper that the implementation defines consistently)? 2) Error code enum: Is there a centralized error code definition (e.g. an AppErrorCode / ErrorType / ErrorCode enum) with meaningful codes like INVALID_PARAMETER, NO_RESOURCE_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS (literal names not required, semantic equivalents acceptable)? 3) Exception hierarchy: Are there custom exception classes (e.g. AppException, BaseAppException, or any project-specific base-exception class) with proper HTTP status mapping? 4) Global error handler: Is there a @ControllerAdvice or WebExceptionHandler (Spring) / ExceptionFilter (NestJS) / middleware error handler (Express/Koa/FastAPI) / equivalent framework primitive that catches and formats all errors? 5) Validation errors: Are framework-level validation errors (e.g. Spring @Valid/@NotNull, class-validator decorators, Zod/Yup schemas, Pydantic models) properly converted to user-friendly messages?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate security practices — CSRF, XSS prevention, input sanitization, secure session management

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate security practices in this low-code platform. Score 0-5 based on: 1) CSRF protection: Is Spring Security CSRF enabled with proper token handling? 2) XSS prevention: Are user inputs sanitized before storage and rendering? Is Content-Security-Policy header set? 3) Session management: Are sessions stored in Redis with proper timeout? Is the SESSION cookie HttpOnly and Secure? 4) Input validation: Are all API inputs validated with bean validation annotations? Are query parameters sanitized to prevent injection? 5) Password security: Are passwords hashed with BCrypt? Is there brute-force protection (rate limiting on login)?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate MongoDB schema design — document structure, indexing strategy, reference patterns

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate MongoDB schema design of this low-code platform. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Document structure: Are entities well-structured with proper field types, defaults, and constraints (@Indexed, @Unique)? 2) Reference strategy: Are related entities referenced by ID (not embedded) for large collections? Is the BaseDomain pattern used for shared fields (createdAt, updatedAt, policies)? 3) Indexing: Are frequently queried fields indexed (e.g. email unique index on User, workspaceId on Application, applicationId on Page/Action)? 4) Soft-delete pattern: Is there a consistent deletedAt/deleted field pattern for recoverable deletes? 5) Audit fields: Do all entities have createdAt, updatedAt auto-populated via @CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate plugin/connector architecture — extensibility, interface design, plugin lifecycle

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the plugin/datasource connector architecture of this low-code platform. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Plugin interface: Is there a well-defined Plugin/Connector interface that all datasource connectors implement (e.g. execute, getStructure, testConnection)? 2) Plugin registry: Is there a PluginExecutor registry that maps plugin types to implementations? 3) Connection pooling: Does each datasource type manage its own connection pool? 4) Plugin metadata: Are plugins self-describing with name, type, icon, supported operations? 5) Extensibility: Can new datasource types be added by implementing the plugin interface without modifying core code?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate widget DSL/layout system — tree structure, widget type coverage, property binding

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the widget DSL and layout system of this low-code platform. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Widget tree DSL: Is the page layout represented as a JSON tree with widgetName, type, children, and dynamic property bindings ({{...}})? 2) Widget type coverage: Are common widget types implemented (Table, Form, Input, Button, Select, Chart, Container, Modal, Tabs)? 3) Property binding: Can widget properties reference other widgets and query results via mustache-style bindings like {{Query1.data}}? 4) Layout system: Is there a grid-based positioning system with row/column coordinates for drag-and-drop? 5) Widget registry: Is there a centralized widget config registry mapping widget types to their default properties, validation rules, and rendering components?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate Git integration implementation — branch management, commit handling, conflict resolution

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the Git integration implementation of this low-code platform. Score 0-4 based on: 1) Git service abstraction: Is there a GitService or GitExecutor that abstracts JGit/Git CLI operations (connect, commit, push, pull, branch)? 2) Application serialization: Are applications serialized to JSON files organized by page/action for clean Git diffs? 3) Branch management: Can users create feature branches, switch between branches, and merge? 4) Conflict detection: Is there handling for merge conflicts and upstream changes (auto-commit, status check)?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate theming system — CSS variable structure, theme switching, custom theme support

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the theming system of this low-code platform. Score 0-4 based on: 1) Theme data model: Are themes stored as structured JSON with color palettes, border radii, box shadows, font families, and density settings? 2) CSS variable integration: Are theme properties applied via CSS custom properties (--var) so all widgets inherit the theme? 3) System vs custom themes: Is there a distinction between built-in system themes (read-only) and user-created custom themes? 4) Live preview: Can users preview theme changes on the canvas before saving/publishing?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate RBAC/permission system design — policy maps, role hierarchy, entity-level access control

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the RBAC/permission system design of this low-code platform. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Policy-based access control: Are permissions defined as policies attached to each entity (policies array with permission + groups)? 2) Role hierarchy: Are default roles (Administrator, Developer, App Viewer) auto-created per workspace with appropriate permission sets? 3) Permission granularity: Are permissions defined at multiple levels (workspace, application, page, datasource) with specific actions (MANAGE, READ, PUBLISH, EXPORT)? 4) Permission check implementation: Is there a centralized policy evaluation service that checks user's group membership against entity policies? 5) Inheritance: Do child entities (pages, actions) inherit permissions from parent (application)?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate query/action editor — query builder UI, parameter binding, response transformation

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the query/action editor implementation of this low-code platform. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Query editor UI: Is there a dedicated editor component for composing database queries and API calls with syntax highlighting? 2) Parameter binding: Can queries reference widget values and other query results via {{mustache}} bindings that are resolved at execution time? 3) Response handling: Is there a structured ActionExecutionResult with isExecutionSuccess, body, headers, and dataTypes? 4) Multiple datasource support: Does the editor adapt its UI based on the selected datasource type (SQL editor for Postgres, JSON editor for MongoDB, form builder for REST)? 5) Run/test functionality: Can users execute queries in edit mode with immediate result preview?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate application import/export system — JSON serialization, partial import, version compatibility

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the application import/export system. Score 0-4 based on: 1) Export format: Is the export a self-contained JSON containing application, pages, actions, datasources, and themes? 2) Import handling: Does import create new entities with fresh IDs while preserving internal references? 3) Datasource handling on import: Are datasource credentials excluded from export by default? Does import prompt for missing credentials? 4) cURL import: Can users import REST API configurations from cURL commands with proper parsing of headers, body, and URL parameters?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate real-time collaboration support — WebSocket, concurrent editing awareness, auto-save

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate real-time collaboration features of this low-code platform. Score 0-4 based on: 1) WebSocket integration: Is there a WebSocket or SSE connection for pushing real-time updates to connected clients? 2) Auto-save: Are page/widget changes auto-saved periodically or on blur? 3) Concurrent editing awareness: Does the system detect when multiple users edit the same page and show indicators or prevent conflicts? 4) Event-driven updates: Are Redis pub/sub or similar mechanisms used to broadcast changes across server instances?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate publish/deploy workflow — draft vs live state management, atomic publish, rollback

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the publish/deploy workflow of this low-code platform. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Dual-state model: Is there a clear separation between draft (unpublished) and live (published) versions of pages, actions, and themes? 2) Atomic publish: Does the publish operation atomically copy all draft state to live state in a single transaction? 3) Published pages array: After publish, does the application have both 'pages' (draft references) and 'livePages' (published snapshots)? 4) Live action state: Do actions maintain a 'liveAction' field that is populated on publish and reflects the published configuration? 5) Unpublished changes indicator: Can the system detect whether there are unpublished changes by comparing draft vs live state?

nodes.description: LLM-Judge: Evaluate multi-tenant data isolation — workspace scoping, cross-tenant access prevention

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate multi-tenant data isolation in this low-code platform. Score 0-5 based on: 1) Workspace scoping: Are all resource queries (applications, pages, actions, datasources) scoped to the current user's workspace? 2) Organization boundary: Is there a tenant/organization layer that prevents cross-organization data access? 3) Policy enforcement: Are entity-level policies checked before every read/write operation? 4) API path scoping: Do API endpoints accept workspaceId and validate user membership? 5) Database-level isolation: Are workspace/organization IDs stored on every document for query filtering?
